newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea central bank union seeks to oust governor.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea central bank union seeks to oust governor.

text.p: South Korea's central bank is likely to lose its supervisory power of the financial industry under a reform proposal and the bank's union on Sunday vowed to oust the governor for agreeing to give up the watchdog role.

A final reform draft by the finance ministry, approved by President Kim Young-sam on Saturday, calls for the setting up of a powerful financial watchdog under the Prime Minister's Office, local media reported.

Details of the draft are due to be released on Monday in a joint news conference by Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik, central bank governor Lee Kyung-shick, and the head of the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform, Park Seong-yawng.
The draft, based on the proposal by the commission and worked out after consultations with the central Bank of Korea, decided not to address the controversial issue of bank ownership.
The commission had proposed granting more autonomy to financial institutions, increasing the central bank's independence and lifting various government regulations.

Under the ministry draft, the banking, insurance and securities supervisory bodies would be merged and report to the prime minister. Currently, the banking watchdog is controlled by the central bank, although the three bodies report ultimately to the finance ministry.
The central bank would only have the right to ask the unified financial watchdog to inspect banks or jointly examine banks, local media said.
The draft is likely to spark protests by central bank officials who have argued that the Bank of Korea should keep supervising banks.
The central bank's trade union said it would launch a campaign to remove governor Lee over the reform.
"We plan to demand the resignation of the governor and start an all-out strike if the supervisory function is taken away from us," said Kim Pil-soo, secretary-general of the union.
"The governor should be held responsible. He has lied to the public and to us by saying he would not give up the regulatory power."
Governor Lee had earlier argued that the central bank should not be deprived of the supervisory role.
Separately, the unions of the three watchdog bodies decided to seek joint action on the reform package. They plan to hold a joint news conference on Tuesday.

Local media reported the final government package failed to raise the limit on bank ownership by individuals. The commission had earlier proposed raising the ceiling to 10 percent from four percent with prior government approval.

Analysts said the government was reluctant to let go of its control of the banking industry because it has a long tradition of controlling large conglomerates, or chaebol, through their access to credit.

"Despite the government's reasoning of a need to prevent a larger concentration of power in an economy, the reform work has failed because it has left room for the government to continue meddling in bank management," the Joong-ang Ilbo newspaper said in an editorial.
The finance ministry is expected to submit the draft to the National Assembly soon.
